recipes.name: Lemony Shrimp over Brown Rice
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Combine the brown rice and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and cook until all the water is absorbed, about 25 minutes.

Melt the butter with the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook the garlic in the butter and oil until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and lemon juice; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer. Stir in the shrimp and cook until the shrimp turns pink, stirring regularly, 5 to 7 minutes. Sprinkle the parsley over the shrimp and cook another 2 minutes. Add the cornstarch to the liquid and stir until it thickens, about 1 minute more. Serve hot over the brown rice.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemony Shrimp over Brown Rice
raw_recipe.description: This shrimp dish was something I threw together one night and my family loved it. It's really easy, healthy, and tasty!

review.reviewBody: On a quest for a new shrimp dish once a week....this recipe was a delight! I added onion and also used cilantro. The Uncle Ben's Boil in a Bag Brown rice was the perfect amount for 1 lb of shrimp to feed 2. Double for 4. Thanks!

I used white rice that I made with saffron. The shrimp were delicious and nothing was left over! Very good and the sauce was great.
For my rice, I like a “fluffy” rice. 
2 tbspns butter. Melt in a skillet, add 1 cup rice and cook until the rice is opaque but do not let it brown. Heat 1/2 cup water in the microwave for 1.5 minutes. Add saffron and let it steep. Heat 1 1/2 cup water in the microwave for 2.5 minutes. When the rice is opaque add the hot water. It is important that the water is hot. This will stop the rice from being sticky. Cover and simmer about 15 to 20 minutes. Keep an eye on it as it gets closer to being done so it does not scorch. It was great with this shrimp.

The whole family liked it.. 2 adults two young kids. Used broth in the rice cooker and have a steam basket on top which I put broccoli and carrots and served together, also added about 1/2 yellow onion with garlic. YUM will make again

I tried this tonite, and OMG!!!! It was WONDERFULLY YUMMY!! I followed the directions but took heed on a couple reviewers...I also like a more soupy sauce, so I added 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth (used that instead of the wine). I had to stop eating so I could have seconds tomorrow! Thanks so much for sharing your recipe...it is a DEFINITE keeper!! :)

Delish! Followed the recipe, except used half wine and half chicken broth. Used half parsley and half cilantro, dried. Sautéed some chopped onion and yellow pepper, before adding the garlic. Served over jasmine rice cooked with chicken broth. The shrimp were perfect, the sauce was yummy. Will make this again.
Cook your rice in chicken broth with slivers of lemon and some med. chopped onion. It adds to over all flavor. Add a little chile flakes to give this a little zing.
Delicious - I added onions in with the garlic, and upped the lemon juice and cilantro (vice parsley). It was so good - and healthy too!
I changed the rice to a more Chinese style with peas, carrots and corn. Added soya sauce

Simple and delicious. If you make this as a main dish, try adding some steamed veggies, i used asparagus and broccoli, and lay them under the shrimp and cover with the same sauce and it is excellent. I also used some hot sauce for a little kick which added a little something as well.

I made this last night with white rice. I added some grated lemon peel (after squeezing the lemon, it seems a shame to throw out the rind), chopped onion and some chopped vegies (broccoli, carrots, cauliflower) and some onion powder, along with some salt and pepper. Fabulous! Also, I didn't pay much attention to exact measurements for ingredients. It didn't seem to matter. This appears to be a very forgiving and flexible recipe. We coupled it with a Sauvignon Blanc and it was heaven!

I sautéed some strips of red bell pepper and onion. Added some minced garlic and dill. My husband doesn't like brown rice so used white. It was tasty, simple and quick. Could probably use more lemon juice and some heat--red pepper flakes or cayenne. I'd make it again.

This is a tasty dish. I made a few tweaks as I cook for one. Omitted the cornstarch as there was not enough liquid for a sauce; added a seeded, minced calabrian chili pepper for a little heat along with chopped parsley to the pan before adding the shrimp. After removing the shrimp from the pan, I put the rice in the pan to collect leftover bits and reheat the rice. I really enjoyed this shrimp and rice meal and will definitely be making it again. Thanks Almondjoy :)
It got a make it again review here from a picky person.
Good but a bit of work deveining the shrimp. We’d prefer over pasta instead of rice. The sauce was a bit thin but tasty.

A really nice dish
It would have been perfect if I had of used real lemon juice

This was so good. I did it with white rice instead of brown rice because my husband is not big on brown rice.
It was so good.
Household favorite! It's quick and easy and you almost feel like a fancy chef while making it!
I added some Old Bay seasoning to it and also some Table Blend Mrs. Dash gave it a nice flavor.
My husband just loved it.
I made it, without the garlic and using quick brown rice, but it was still easy and very tasty. Will be having it again many times.
